candidate.title: Average-Case Hardness of Planted k-Orthogonal Vectors
candidate.subtitle: A planting that preserves every marginal below k, proposed as a basis for fine-grained cryptography
candidate.one_line: No algorithm solves the planted decision k-OV problem with constant success probability above 1/2 in time O(n^(k-eps)).
candidate.status_note: Conjecture 10 of the source, and a newly proposed average-case assumption rather than a question the literature already asked. Its worst-case counterpart -- that k-OV requires n^(k-o(1)) time -- is a central conjecture of fine-grained complexity.
candidate.progress_note: The planting preserves the marginal distribution of any subset of strictly fewer than k vectors, so nothing below arity k can distinguish planted from model instances. The source also gives a search-to-decision reduction (Theorem 12) for alpha(n) = polylog(n).

check.notes: Conjecture 10 is verbatim on page 11 and needed no repair. Two things are recorded rather than assumed. First, the statement says explicitly what kind of claim this is -- a newly proposed assumption awaiting cryptanalysis, published because the underlying object is canonical and the planting is analysed rather than merely asserted, not because the literature had posed it. Second, a parameter mismatch the source does not flag: the conjecture is stated for alpha = omega(1) while the search-to-decision reduction requires alpha = polylog(n), so a resolution should say which regime it addresses.
